PO5.115
A Videography Documented Case Report:
Antibody-Negative Stiff-Person Syndrome Joanna S.
Fong, Derk Krieger, Cleveland, OH
OBJECTIVE: Our aim is to further characterize antibody-negative Stiff-
Person Syndrome and to demonstrate its responsiveness to plasmapheresis.
BACKGROUND: Stiff-Person Syndrome (SPS) is a rare neurologic disor-
der of which only 150 cases have been reported in the past twenty-five
years. It is well recognized as an autoimmune disease directed against
synaptic antigens which causes progressive rigidity and muscle spasms.
Multiple antigens have been identified, including the GABA-synthesizing
enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD), and others such as amphiphy-
sin and gephyrin. DESIGN/METHODS: We report the case of a 37 year-
old Caucasian man with a history of rheumatoid arthritis under treatment
with anti-tumor necrosis factor agents, who presented with a six-year his-
tory of progressive muscle spasms and rigidity. RESULTS: Clinical presen-
tation was most consistent with SPS, however, laboratory testing for anti-
GAD, anti-amphiphysin, CRMP-5 western blot, and VGKC antibody tests
were negative. The patient displayed a dramatic clinical response to plas-
mapheresis (5 treatments over 2 weeks), which was documented by videog-
raphy. CONCLUSIONS/RELEVANCE: This strongly suggests that SPS
is an antibody-mediated disease for which all pathogenetic antibodies are
yet to be described. Although ancillary tests such as antibody testing and
EMG are useful, the diagnosis can largely be made based on clinical pre-
sentation and response to therapy.
